This implies that Cephalexin may exert its effects on bacterial infections, which can manifest as prostatitis in certain cases. The indirect pathway highlights a potential mechanism where Cephalexin's antibacterial activity could contribute to the development of prostatitis, though the exact mechanism remains unclear. The evidence supports a relationship between Cephalexin and Prostatitis through a chain of indications, suggesting a possible role in bacterial infection-related pathophysiology.
